**Sepsis 1-Hour Bundle (Boundaries & Exclusions)** ★★ — Cultures + lactate → IV antibiotics ==≤1 h== (never delayed >45 min) + ==30 mL/kg== balanced crystalloids + norepinephrine (MAP ==≥65 mmHg==); obey every "only/unless/never" boundary.

- **Flow:** Suspect sepsis → lactate + ≥2 blood cultures (==never== delay abx >==45 min==) → IV abx ==≤1 h== (3 h ==only if== possible without shock) → balanced crystalloids ==≥30 mL/kg== (≤3 h) + early norepinephrine if MAP <65 → refractory shock → add vasopressin ==≤0.03 U/min== + hydrocortisone ==200 mg/day==.

## Strict boundaries (Do not / Only / Unless) ★★

| Intervention | Rule | Exact restriction / exception |
|---|---|---|
| **Antimicrobials** ★★ | Within ==1 hour== (shock / likely sepsis) | ==3 h== ==only if== sepsis possible ==without shock==; ==never== delay >==45 min== for cultures |
| **Antifungals / dual GNB** | ==Do not== add/continue routinely | Antifungals ==unless== high fungal risk; stop dual GNB once susceptibilities known ==except== resistant pathogens |
| **Fluids** ★★ | ==≥30 mL/kg== balanced crystalloids ≤3 h (lactate ==≥4 mmol/L== or hypotension) | ==Do not use hydroxyethyl starches under any circumstance==; ==do not== rely on CVP alone (use dynamic vars) |
| **Norepinephrine** ★★ | First-line, target MAP ==≥65 mmHg== | ==Do not withhold== waiting for fluid bolus if MAP <65; peripheral ==only while== obtaining central access |
| **Vasopressin** ★ | Up to ==0.03 units/min== | ==Only as second-line adjunct==, ==never== first-line monotherapy |
| **Dopamine** ★ | ==Never use== | ==Unless== symptomatic bradycardia with low tachyarrhythmia risk |
| **Hydrocortisone** ★ | ==200 mg/day== IV | ==Only for refractory septic shock==; ==do not== give routinely in sepsis ==without shock== |
| **Sodium bicarbonate** ★★ | ==Do not give== for lactic acidaemia haemodynamics | ==Unless== arterial pH ==≤7.15== AND **AKI (AKIN stage 2-3)** |
| **RBC transfusion** ★ | Transfuse ==only when Hb <7.0 g/dL== | ==Unless== active haemorrhage, acute myocardial ischaemia, or severe hypoxaemia |

## ⚠ Never (polarity critical)

- ==Never== delay antimicrobials ==more than 45 minutes== for blood cultures.
- ==Do not== use **hydroxyethyl starches** under any circumstance (↑renal injury, ↑mortality).
- ==Do not== rely on **CVP alone** for fluid responsiveness.
- ==Do not== withhold vasopressors while completing 30 mL/kg fluids if MAP ==<65 mmHg== persists.
- ==Never== use **vasopressin** as first-line monotherapy or **dopamine** (unless bradycardic + low tachyarrhythmia risk).
- ==Do not== give routine **hydrocortisone** without shock or **bicarbonate** (unless pH ≤7.15 + AKIN 2-3).

## Cards

- Maximum permissible culture delay and antibiotic timing windows in sepsis → Never delay antibiotics >45 min; give IV antimicrobials ≤1 h for shock/likely sepsis, and within 3 h ONLY if sepsis is possible without shock
- Which resuscitation fluid is strictly forbidden in sepsis and why? → Hydroxyethyl starches — never use under any circumstance (increase renal injury and mortality)
- Should vasopressors wait until the 30 mL/kg fluid bolus finishes? → No; do not withhold vasopressors if life-threatening hypotension (MAP <65 mmHg) persists
- Exact role restrictions for norepinephrine, vasopressin, and dopamine → Norepinephrine first-line (MAP ≥65 mmHg; peripheral only while obtaining central access); vasopressin ≤0.03 U/min ONLY second-line, never first-line; NEVER dopamine unless symptomatic bradycardia with low tachyarrhythmia risk
- When is IV hydrocortisone (200 mg/day) indicated in sepsis? → Only for refractory septic shock requiring ongoing vasopressors; do not give routinely in sepsis without shock
- When is sodium bicarbonate allowed in sepsis-induced lactic acidaemia? → Do not give unless arterial pH ≤7.15 with AKI (AKIN stage 2 or 3)
- RBC transfusion threshold and its three exceptions → Transfuse only when Hb <7.0 g/dL, unless active haemorrhage, acute myocardial ischaemia, or severe hypoxaemia
